Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE), Greece: basic VAT rates (24% standard in force since 1 June 2016; 30% island reduction)
Tax Foundation: 2022 VAT Rates in Europe (table as of January 2022, sourced from the European Commission's Taxes in Europe Database)

caveats: individualTaxYear is the calendar year, inferred from the country's annual assessment cycle (grade I); not confirmed on the authority's own pages in this pass.
companyYearEndDefault is a 31 December app default for new entities (grade I), not a statutory requirement; companies may choose other year ends under national law.
Greece lists three reduced rates (6 / 13 / 17) in the Commission's table; the authority site (aade.gr) was blocked to automated fetches this session.

The 24% standard rate has applied since 1 June 2016 (AADE). The 30% island reduction (17% / 9% / 4%) predates the coverage window but its start date was not sourced, so those rows carry lower-bound dates; from 1 January 2026 Law 5246/2025 extended the reduction to further small Aegean and Dodecanese islands - a scope change, not a rate change.

Lower-bound rows - reduced (2022-01-01), reduced2 (2022-01-01), superReduced (2022-01-01): the `from` date is the earliest a source confirms the rate applied, not necessarily its true start (confirmed applying on 1 January 2022 by the Tax Foundation's January 2022 table of VAT rates (sourced from the Commission's Taxes in Europe Database)).
